claim.pdf_says:
=    Relational operator - equal
       and assignment operator in COMPUTE
==   Pseudo-text delimiter in COPY and REPLACE statements
claim.markdown_says:
| = | Relational operator - equal |

and assignment operator in COMPUTE

| == | Pseudo-text delimiter in COPY and REPLACE statements |
|---|---|
claim.why_it_matters: The '=' row of the special character words table loses its second meaning ('and assignment operator in COMPUTE'), which is detached as a loose paragraph that splits the table in two; the second table fragment then starts with '==' as its header row.

verdict.reasoning: Printed page 107 (ISO/IEC 1989:2014 p.83, 8.3.1.1.3.1) shows one continuous Word/Meaning table; the '=' entry's meaning wraps onto an indented continuation line 'and assignment operator in COMPUTE' within the Meaning column, immediately followed by the '==' row. The markdown ends the table after '| = | Relational operator - equal |', emits the continuation as a standalone paragraph, then opens a second table whose HEADER row is '| == | Pseudo-text delimiter ... |' followed by '|---|---|'. Both quotes in the claim match the sources exactly. The words are all present, but the structure changes meaning: the COMPUTE-assignment meaning is no longer attached to '=' (it reads as free text), and '==' becomes a column header rather than a special-character-word entry, so any reader or tool consuming the table loses the '=' assignment meaning and the '==' word. This is a genuine structural transcription defect, not mere wrapping.
